quizzes.title: Unix to Linux
quizzes.goal: Easy facts: kernel versus distro, history, licenses.

questions.title: Year
questions.prompt: Unix work at Bell Labs is usually dated to around which year?
questions.explanation: Thompson and Ritchie were building Unix at Bell Labs around 1969.

questions.title: Kernel
questions.prompt: In the strict sense, Linux is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Linux is the kernel. Distributions bundle it with userland and packaging.

questions.title: GNU
questions.prompt: GNU's historical gap, which Linux filled, was mainly:
questions.explanation: GNU had userland tools but not a finished kernel. Linux supplied one.

questions.title: Distro
choices: The Linux kernel with a different name
A distribution that includes a Linux kernel
questions.explanation: Ubuntu is a distro: kernel plus userland plus packaging and defaults.

questions.title: People
questions.prompt: Who announced the Linux kernel in 1991?
questions.explanation: Linus Torvalds announced the kernel he was writing for his 386.

questions.title: C
questions.prompt: Unix was rewritten in C primarily because:
choices: C made the system more portable than assembly
questions.explanation: C let Unix be structured and ported without staying in assembly.

questions.title: Pipe
choices: Standard output of one process to standard input of another
questions.explanation: The kernel copies bytes from one process's stdout to the next stdin.

questions.title: POSIX
choices: A portable Unix-like API and utility contract
questions.explanation: POSIX is a standard for Unix-like interfaces, not a kernel.

questions.title: GPL
questions.prompt: The Linux kernel's GPLv2 license is an example of:
questions.explanation: GPL is copyleft: distributed modifications must offer corresponding source.

questions.title: Permissive
questions.prompt: An MIT or BSD license typically allows:
questions.explanation: Permissive licenses allow proprietary derivatives, unlike GPL copyleft.

questions.title: Philosophy
choices: One large program that does everything
Small programs that compose over text streams
questions.explanation: McIlroy's summary: small tools, composition, text streams.

questions.title: Name fight
questions.prompt: People say GNU/Linux when they want to stress that:
choices: Much of the userland is GNU, while Linux is the kernel
questions.explanation: The phrase highlights GNU userland plus the Linux kernel.

questions.title: Bell
questions.explanation: Bell Labs is the origin of Unix.

questions.title: Not VM
questions.prompt: lilC's Linux course teaches Linux ideas without:
choices: Shipping a remote Linux VM in the app
questions.explanation: The app does not include SSH or a VM. Study is offline content.

questions.title: Ritchie
questions.prompt: Dennis Ritchie is closely associated with:
choices: The C language and early Unix
questions.explanation: Ritchie designed C and co-created Unix.

questions.title: Variant
questions.prompt: Vendor Unix variants in the 1980s helped motivate:
questions.explanation: Splintered Unix APIs were a reason to write POSIX.

questions.title: Userland
choices: Part of the Linux kernel binary
questions.explanation: They run in user space. The kernel is a separate artifact.

questions.title: apt
questions.prompt: If a tutorial says apt install, it is assuming:
questions.explanation: apt is Debian/Ubuntu packaging, not a kernel feature.

questions.title: Kernel job
questions.prompt: Which task is the kernel's, not bash's?
questions.explanation: Scheduling is kernel work. Globbing and quotes are shell work.

questions.title: Distractor
choices: A distro includes a kernel and much more
Linux is another name for GNU coreutils
questions.explanation: coreutils is userland. Linux is not a synonym for GNU tools.

questions.title: Mode
questions.prompt: User processes normally cannot program devices directly because:
choices: The CPU privilege split and kernel mediation prevent it
questions.explanation: Hardware access is privileged. The kernel mediates via drivers and syscalls.

questions.title: Syscall
questions.prompt: Which of these is a system call rather than a libc convenience?
questions.explanation: write is a syscall (or a very thin wrapper). printf formats then may write.

questions.title: printf
questions.prompt: printf typically reaches the kernel by eventually calling:
questions.explanation: Formatted output is buffered in user space, then written.

questions.title: Process
choices: An address space, credentials, and file descriptors
questions.explanation: Isolation is the point: private memory, own fd table, own uid.

questions.title: pid1
questions.explanation: The kernel starts userspace at pid 1.

questions.title: VFS
questions.prompt: The virtual filesystem exists so that:
choices: Disks, pipes, and /proc can share open/read/write
questions.explanation: VFS is the common file API over many backends.

questions.title: proc
choices: A real file stored on the root disk inode for CPU firmware
questions.explanation: /proc is a kernel filesystem, not a place you store documents.

questions.title: malloc
questions.prompt: malloc gets more memory from the OS using:
choices: Direct access to another process's heap
Kernel interfaces such as brk or mmap
questions.explanation: The allocator asks the kernel for address space.

questions.title: Driver
questions.explanation: Drivers typically need privileged hardware access.

questions.title: Root
choices: A user process with all-powerful credentials
questions.explanation: Root is still userspace, with uid 0.

questions.title: Socket
questions.prompt: Sending a TCP packet is performed by:
choices: The process writing directly to the NIC registers in portable C
The kernel network stack on behalf of a socket
questions.explanation: The process uses a socket; the kernel owns the stack.

questions.title: strace
choices: System calls a process actually makes

questions.title: Layer
questions.prompt: 'Command not found' is usually a failure of:
questions.explanation: The shell could not resolve an executable name.

questions.title: Layer2
questions.prompt: 'Permission denied' on open is decided by:
choices: Kernel credential checks on a VFS object

questions.title: ABI
questions.prompt: The Linux syscall ABI is closest to which language's data model?

questions.title: Isolate
choices: To give each process a private address space
questions.explanation: Isolation and a convenient linear address space.

questions.title: ioctl
questions.explanation: ioctl is the classic grab-bag for device ops.

questions.title: Not kernel
questions.prompt: Which is not a kernel job?
choices: Expanding unquoted globs in a command line

questions.title: Cake
questions.prompt: From the bottom, a fair layering is:
questions.explanation: Hardware, then kernel, then libc, then shell, then applications.

questions.prompt: A student's own files usually belong in:

questions.title: proc
choices: A kernel interface mounted as files

questions.title: inode
choices: A name and a pointer to an inode
questions.explanation: The inode holds metadata and data locations.

questions.title: Hard
choices: Is a second name for the same inode on one filesystem
Is another name for a mount
questions.explanation: Hard links share an inode and stay on one filesystem.

questions.title: Soft
choices: A duplicate inode of the target
questions.explanation: A symlink is a path, which may dangle.

questions.title: rm
choices: Removes a directory entry; data lasts until last link and last fd go
questions.explanation: Unlink removes a name, not necessarily the data yet.

questions.title: bin
questions.prompt: User command binaries commonly live in:

questions.title: dev
choices: A device node, still opened as a file descriptor

questions.title: traverse
questions.prompt: Execute permission on a directory means:
choices: You may traverse to a known name inside it
You may always list all names

questions.title: mount
choices: Attaches that filesystem at a directory in the tree
questions.explanation: Mount grafts a tree onto a directory.

questions.title: local
questions.prompt: Locally built software is conventionally placed in:

questions.title: bytes
questions.explanation: No record format in the filesystem.

questions.title: Mixup
questions.prompt: Where does a typical system log belong?

questions.title: What
choices: A user program that runs other programs

questions.title: PATH
questions.prompt: A command name with no slash is found via:
questions.explanation: PATH is a list of directories to search.

questions.title: slash
choices: POSIX requires it to be bash
questions.explanation: A slash means it is a pathname, not a PATH search.

questions.title: cd
questions.prompt: cd must be a shell builtin because:
choices: Only the shell process's cwd should change
questions.explanation: An external cd would only change a child.

questions.title: argv
questions.prompt: After the shell parses the line, the program receives:
questions.explanation: Quotes are shell syntax, not program input.

questions.title: single
choices: Inhibit expansion and pass characters literally
questions.explanation: Single quotes are the literal shield.

questions.title: double
questions.prompt: In bash, "$file" is preferred over $file because:
choices: It prevents word-splitting and globbing of the value
It makes the variable an integer
questions.explanation: Quote expansions that are filenames or data.

questions.title: not found
choices: The disk is in kernel mode
No executable matched PATH or the name was wrong

questions.title: builtin
questions.prompt: Which is typically a shell builtin?
questions.explanation: cd must change the shell itself.

questions.title: hidden
questions.prompt: A glob * does not match names starting with . unless:
choices: The pattern itself starts with a dot (or you set options to include them)
questions.explanation: Dotfiles are excluded from * by default.

questions.title: type
questions.prompt: In bash, type ls tells you:
choices: Whether ls is an alias, builtin, or file

questions.title: child
questions.prompt: The executed program does not see your quotes because:
choices: The shell parsed the line first

questions.title: Trap
choices: Two arguments a and b, after splitting

questions.title: pwd
questions.prompt: You want to know where you are. You run:

questions.title: dot
choices: Names starting with . are omitted from default ls

questions.title: page
questions.prompt: To page through a long file, prefer:
questions.explanation: less is a pager. cat dumps everything.

questions.title: tail
choices: Following a file as it grows

questions.title: touch
choices: Create file if missing and update timestamps

questions.title: mv
questions.prompt: On the same filesystem, mv is often:
choices: A full byte copy plus delete
questions.explanation: Rename is cheap on one fs.

questions.title: rm
choices: Typically refuses because the name is a directory

questions.title: hyphen
questions.prompt: A file named -r should be referred to as:

questions.prompt: A name with a space should be:

questions.prompt: You mean to rename a.c to b.c. Prefer:
choices: cp a.c b.c && rm a.c always, even on one filesystem

choices: Know that the directory exists if you already have its name? wait — you cannot traverse into it

questions.title: chown
choices: Giving away or taking files is a privileged operation
It is a bash builtin that cannot fail

questions.title: sudo
choices: As another user, often root, according to policy

questions.prompt: kill pid with no signal name sends:

choices: It cannot be caught or ignored

questions.title: zombie
choices: Dead, waiting for the parent to collect its status

questions.title: ctrlc
questions.prompt: Ctrl-C in an interactive shell typically sends:

questions.title: bg
questions.prompt: Placing & at the end of a command:

questions.title: export
choices: Marks VAR for inheritance by child processes

choices: Truncates or creates out.txt and sends stdout there

questions.title: order

questions.title: order2
choices: The original stdout (often the terminal), not out

questions.title: pipe
choices: a's stderr to b's stdin always
a and b to the same inode

questions.title: both run
choices: Always run strictly one after the other with no overlap
Run concurrently, connected by a kernel buffer

choices: *.c is a regular expression evaluated by grep by default
*.c is a shell glob for filenames
grep expands globs instead of the shell

questions.title: tee
choices: Copies stdout to a file and still passes it along

questions.title: diag
questions.prompt: Progress messages in a filter should go to:

quizzes.title: Network concepts
quizzes.goal: IP, port, DNS, ICMP, SSH as an idea.

questions.title: IP
choices: An interface address on a network

questions.prompt: Port 22 is the conventional port for:

questions.title: DNS
choices: Inodes to names on one disk

questions.title: hosts

questions.title: loop

questions.title: ping fail
choices: Not necessarily; ICMP may be dropped while TCP works
questions.explanation: ICMP is not the whole story.

questions.title: ssh
choices: A Linux kernel subsystem required to boot
A protocol for encrypted remote login and tunnels
questions.explanation: A protocol. lilC does not session it.

questions.title: lilc
choices: An SSH session to a hidden VM
No remote Linux VM; this module is conceptual

questions.title: daemon

The kernel has no IP stack

questions.title: split

IP = machine/interface identity, port = service conversation

questions.title: shebang

the NIC which port to bind

questions.title: plusx
